extracted.intended_audience: NIH peer reviewers, study section chairs, and Scientific Review Officers (reviewers of NIH Research Project Grant applications)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for reviewers evaluating Research Project Grant (RPG) applications under NIH's Simplified Review Framework, including how the five regulatory review criteria are reorganized into three Factors, how those Factors are scored/evaluated, and how they feed into the Overall Impact score.

rubrics_metrics.name: Significance
rubrics_metrics.description: One of the five regulatory criteria retained under the simplified review framework: Significance, Investigators, Innovation, Approach, Environment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The page states Significance is retained as a regulatory review criterion but that the five criteria are reorganized into three Factors under the simplified framework. Significance will be considered (as part of the relevant Factor) in arriving at the Overall Impact score. See linked Reviewer Guide and Scoring Guidance for detailed evaluation expectations and examples.

rubrics_metrics.name: Investigators
rubrics_metrics.description: One of the five regulatory criteria retained under the simplified review framework: Significance, Investigators, Innovation, Approach, Environment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Investigators remains a core regulatory review criterion and is incorporated into the three-Factor structure; it will be considered in arriving at the Overall Impact. Detailed reviewer expectations (e.g., qualifications, team composition) are provided in the Reviewer Guide to Evaluating Applications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Innovation
rubrics_metrics.description: One of the five regulatory criteria retained under the simplified review framework: Significance, Investigators, Innovation, Approach, Environment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Innovation is maintained as a regulatory criterion and is folded into the three Factors. Reviewers should consult the Reviewer Guide and Scoring Guidance for how Innovation is weighed and scored under the simplified framework.

rubrics_metrics.name: Approach
rubrics_metrics.description: One of the five regulatory criteria retained under the simplified review framework: Significance, Investigators, Innovation, Approach, Environment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Approach remains a fundamental review criterion (methods, rigor, feasibility) and is reorganized into one of the three Factors. Approach-related evaluation and scoring examples are available in the Scoring Guidance and Reviewer Guide documents linked on the page.

rubrics_metrics.name: Environment
rubrics_metrics.description: One of the five regulatory criteria retained under the simplified review framework: Significance, Investigators, Innovation, Approach, Environment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Environment (institutional resources, support) is retained and incorporated into the three-Factor model; reviewers should assess sufficiency/adequacy as described in the Reviewer Guide and related materials.

rubrics_metrics.name: Three Factors (reorganization of five regulatory criteria)
rubrics_metrics.description: The simplified review framework reorganizes the five regulatory criteria into three Factors which will be considered during review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifically: Factors 1 and 2 will receive numerical criterion scores and Factor 3 will be evaluated for sufficiency. All three Factors will be considered in arriving at the Overall Impact score. (The page refers reviewers to the Simplified Peer Review Framework and linked documents for the mapping of the five criteria into the three Factors and for detailed guidance on each Factor.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Factor scoring vs. sufficiency (Factors 1, 2, and 3)
rubrics_metrics.description: Scoring rules for the new Factor structure under the simplified review framework.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Factors 1 and 2: receive numerical criterion scores. Factor 3: evaluated for sufficiency (not given a numerical criterion score). All Factors nonetheless feed into the Overall Impact determination. See the Scoring Guidance PDF and Reviewer Guide to Evaluating Applications for examples and scoring instructions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Overall Impact score
rubrics_metrics.description: The Overall Impact score is the final assessment for an application and is arrived at by considering the three Factors together along with Additional Review Criteria.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers should consider Factors 1–3 and the Additional Review Criteria when assigning the Overall Impact. The Reviewer Guide and Scoring Guidance provide examples of how Factors and Additional Criteria are synthesized into an Overall Impact assessment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Additional Review Criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: Additional Review Criteria are evaluated along with the three Factors and are part of what is considered in determining the Overall Impact score.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The page notes that Additional Review Criteria are considered alongside the Factors in arriving at Overall Impact. Some Additional Review Considerations (see next entry) are being shifted from reviewer assessment to NIH staff review; reviewers should consult the guidance documents for specific expectations about which Additional Criteria they must evaluate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Additional Review Considerations shifted to NIH staff (Applications from Foreign Organizations; Select Agents; Resource Sharing Plans)
rubrics_metrics.description: Certain Additional Review Considerations — specifically Applications from Foreign Organizations, Select Agents, and Resource Sharing Plans — are being shifted from reviewers to NIH staff.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because review responsibility for these considerations is being shifted to NIH staff, reviewers will not be required to evaluate these items in their criterion scoring. Reviewers should be aware these items remain part of the application assessment but will be handled by staff; see the Simplified Peer Review Framework and linked resources for details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewer Guide to Evaluating Applications (resource)
rubrics_metrics.description: A linked document titled 'Reviewer Guide to Evaluating Applications' that 'provides guidance on evaluating and scoring applications under the simplified review framework.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This PDF (linked on the page) contains detailed instructions, expectations, and examples for how reviewers should evaluate applications under the new framework. Reviewers are directed to this guide for specifics beyond the high-level summary on the web page.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scoring Guidance (resource)
rubrics_metrics.description: A linked 'Scoring Guidance' document that 'provides an overview of the approach to scoring under the simplified review framework, with accompanying examples.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This document summarizes how numerical scoring is to be applied to Factors 1 and 2, how Factor 3 sufficiency is evaluated, and gives worked examples. Reviewers should use it when assigning criterion scores and Overall Impact.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewer and Chair Discussion / Critique Presentation Guidance (cheat sheets and videos)
rubrics_metrics.description: Documents and videos (Reviewer Discussion Cheat Sheet, Chair Discussion Cheat Sheet, Chair Orientation Video, Discussion excerpts) that guide reviewers and chairs through the meeting discussion process and critique presentation under the simplified framework.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These resources provide practical guidance on conducting panel discussions, presenting critiques, and fulfilling roles (reviewer vs. chair) under the simplified framework. They include orientation materials, suggested discussion flow, and tips for critique presentation; reviewers and chairs are advised to consult these before meetings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewer Training Materials (slides, orientation videos)
rubrics_metrics.description: Training slides and orientation recordings designed to prepare reviewers and chairs for reviewing and scoring under the simplified review framework.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Materials include an introduction video to the Simplified Review Framework, incoming chair orientations, and a slide deck for SRO-led orientation sessions. These resources explain the rationale for the change, expected reviewer behavior, and illustrate scoring and discussion practices with examples.
